question: Should Crabline adopt these provider-native behavior corrections as unconditional replacements for its existing mock behavior after representative client validation?
rationale: Repository policy favors native fidelity, but this branch changes observable contracts across several providers and recorder failure semantics; source review and green focused tests cannot determine whether existing Crabline consumers depend on the previous behavior.

options.title: Validate Then Land
options.body: Remove the changelog entry, correct the scope description, and confirm representative native-client flows for the highest-risk Telegram, Mattermost, Signal, WhatsApp, and recorder paths before merging.

options.title: Accept Tested Risk
options.body: Merge based on the focused test suite while explicitly accepting that consumers relying on prior mock quirks may need updates.

options.title: Split The Bundle
options.body: Separate recorder durability from provider-specific protocol changes so each compatibility boundary can be reviewed independently.

recommendation.title: Validate Then Land
recommendation.body: Remove the changelog entry, correct the scope description, and confirm representative native-client flows for the highest-risk Telegram, Mattermost, Signal, WhatsApp, and recorder paths before merging.
